title: Winner's Curse
hook: You won the bidding war. That might be the bad news.
statement: When you beat everyone in a bidding war, it usually means you overestimated the value the most.
explainer: When lots of people guess the value of something uncertain, the winner is usually the most optimistic one. Winning itself is a hint you paid too much.
sop: Set your own value before you see anyone else's bid.
Figure out what other serious bidders are likely offering.
Subtract the Average Bid from your planned Winning Bid.
Shade your bid down to account for being the optimist.
Walk away if winning means going past your number.
equation_example: Winning Bid $1,200,000 minus Average Bid $900,000 = $300,000 of likely overpayment. A big gap means you were the outlier optimist. A bid near the average means the crowd's estimate backs you up.
question: Before your next deal, write down your walk-away number before you see any other offers.
closing_statement: Know what it's worth to you. Ignore the thrill of winning.
caption:
Principle Nº 343: Winner's Curse

You won the bidding war. That might be the bad news.

When you beat everyone in a bidding war, it usually means you overestimated the value the most.

Your turn: Before your next deal, write down your walk-away number before you see any other offers.
